correctness.rationale: The complete proof derives the k3 coefficient polynomial by exact summation, establishes a unimodular reduction of the full coefficient ideal to gcd(A,B,C) and the first three terms, and evaluates all prime exponents including p=2 and p=3 without numerical assumptions. The standalone checker verified 7,996 parameter branches and 204 independent coin-change coefficient comparisons. Limits: arithmetic checks alone do not prove infinity; the symbolic steps do.

originality.rationale: The closest 2001 paper proves the same four lower-bound congruences and supplies the operator factorization, but not the maximal common divisors or exceptional factor-3 profile. The 2017 enumeration paper and 2024 general congruence work do not cover this quantified exactness. Searches of published records and semantic mathematical index found no equal or stronger covering statement. This does not certify absolute novelty.
residual_risks: An unindexed publication might already explicitly derive the sharp all-n four-branch gcd from the published operator recurrences.
The arithmetic proof at depth three is a specific consequence of the known series decomposition, so it does not imply novelty at larger depths.

value.rationale: The exact optimal uniform modulus is the natural invariant left undetermined by known m-ary branch congruence theorems. All four branches and every base m>=2 are classified, with a genuinely arithmetic mod-nine exceptional phase, and a finite 3-term certificate for the infinite gcd. The result is a complete exact classification rather than a one-off congruence or an arbitrary numerical sample.
